newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - RANK RAISES SHARE BUY-BACK PLAN.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - RANK RAISES SHARE BUY-BACK PLAN.

text.p: British leisure group Rank Group Plc has raised plans to buy back its own shares and the repurchase will start in the next few days, said chief executive Andrew Teare in an interview on Thursday.
"We will commence the share buy back programme in the next few days. Originally we said we would buy back up to 250 million (pounds), we are now saying it will be up to 10 percent," said Teare.
At the group's last annual meeting, shareholders gave their approval for a buy-back of up to a maximum 10 percent of shares in issue, a mandate which lasts for this financial year.

Teare, who joined Rank in April 1996, has raised 1.3 billion pounds from disposals, including the sale of the group's remaining 20 percent stake in the Rank Xerox office equipment venture to Xerox Corporation XRN.N in a deal worth up to 1.0 billion pounds.
"We have said that as we get further Xerox proceeds we will take decisions, as cash arises, in terms of our buyback programme," said Teare.

Rank shares, which have under-performed the market by some 40 percent over the last year, fell a further 26 pence to 347p in early trade after the group announced a larger than expected drop in first half profits.
But Teare defended his strategy for re-focusing the group on four core areas -- film and entertainment services, Hard Rock cafes, holidays and leisure.

"We believe our strategy is absolutely right for this business. When it was announced twelve months ago we said we will sell peripheral businesses to the value of about 300 million in two years, and we finished that in eight months.

"We said we would resolve the dilemma of the Rank Xerox investment and we solved that in June. We said we would focus on leisure and entertainment and that is exactly what we have done by that disposal programme," he added.
The company is in the middle of the fourth and fifth parts of the strategy, revitalising the management team and making the business more focused, said Teare.
Earlier, Rank announced a 12 million stg drop to 87 million in its pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits in the six months ended June 30, hit by very weak video duplication sales in the United States.

In video duplication, U.S. sales fell by 22 percent due to a low level of major video releases by Rank's major customers. But Teare said the group was confident of a return to its strongest ever video release pattern in the second half.
"It is likely to be the strongest return to video release pattern we have ever had," said Teare.

"While we can't talk about all the titles that will come, because the studios haven't announced them yet, the second half has kicked off with two big titles -- Liar Liar, and the new run of the Star Wars trilogy.
"So we are very confident on video in the second half."

Trading profit from its film and entertainment division fell by 31 percent to 20 million in the first half. Profits from Rank's Hard Rock cafe chain rose five percent to 20 million and the group's leisure division which includes Odeon cinemas and a chain of Tom Cobleigh restaurant pubs improved profits by 12 percent to 47 million stg.
The holiday division which includes Butlin's holiday camps in Britain increased profits by 2.0 million to 8.0 million.
Summer holiday bookings are currently up by two percent in volume and 11 percent in value, said the company.
